issues.claim: The epoch-spread mutation's timing and decision rule disagree between the base and V06. Base §4.11 *The epoch-spread mutation (item 18 (c))* still reads "the engine issues §4.7 S11's `MutationRecord` as a sequence of `mutate` events over the ladder's rung durations (item 31) … Each of those events decides and records its step at once", and `UseConversionOp`'s `mutate.spread` comment reads "'epochs' issues its steps over the ladder's durations". V06 §3.10.1 (the engine, the only issuer of a spread) decides the whole record once at the creating op, splits its parts into occupy · adapt · extend · rebuild steps due at `mutation.stepYears` (V06 §2.2: occupy 0 · adapt [1, 3] · extend [3, 10] · rebuild [8, 25]) and states "these rows replace the base's 'over the ladder's rung durations'"; it also opens the use at the first compatible step (`opensAt`), lays an always-crypt target's crypt at occupy, and applies the inverse of the done steps when a cancelled plan's building takes its former designation (item 18 (e)). f item 266 (BCR-V6-21) is the ruled base change that carries exactly this text; it is not in the base. A builder following the base schedules each step on the `WealthLadderTable` years and re-decides each step; V06 schedules on its own rows from one record — two generators. (The canon routed f item 266 to model, by the f file's §2.8 heading; its text edits §4.11, the pipeline's.)
issues.required_change: At pipeline, §4.11 *The epoch-spread mutation*: Apply f item 266 as written: "§4.7 S11's `MutationRecord`, decided once at the creating op, as a sequence of `mutate` events each applying its own parts of that record, due at the evolution table's `mutation.stepYears` rows (V06 §2.2) — first occupy, when the present design is compatible (every kept part, nothing added; an always-crypt target's crypt basement exempt and laid then); otherwise the use opens at the first step whose result is compatible, a relocating use staying at its former site until then; then adapt; then extend (the adds); and rebuild only the parts that cannot be adapted. A plan cancelled because its use left keeps its done steps; when the building next takes its former designation, the mutator's record is the inverse of the done steps (item 18 (e))", and "Each of those events applies and records its step at once"; the record and its rules pointing to V06 §2.5, §3.10. In `UseConversionOp`, `spread`'s comment reads "'epochs' issues its steps at `mutation.stepYears` (V06 §2.2, §3.10)".

issues.claim: Base §4.11 *The runner* says V06's `'history'` strategy "adds the steps `prelude`, `hazards`, `fortification`, `terrainWater`, `raisedWays`, `close` and the participant steps at V06 §3.2's places". Against V06 §2.1's twenty-step `EpochStep` and V06 §3.1 (2) / §3.2 this list is wrong both ways: `prelude` is a `'grow-by-stage'` phase already (the base names it among the nine, and V06 §3.1 (2) reuses it as "`prelude`'s base part"), while the engine's own steps `uses` ((b)), `departures` and `decline` ((c)) and `ladder` ((d)) are missing — the base itself states that the use step, the strike pool and the ladder's schedule are the staged engine's, not `'grow-by-stage'`'s. A reader of the base cannot tell which steps run under which strategy.
issues.required_change: At pipeline, §4.11 *The runner*: Restore f item 317's subject and make the list exact: "The epoch's order (a)–(j) gains the steps `prelude`, `hazards`, `fortification`, `terrainWater`, `raisedWays`, `close` and the participant steps `afterField`, `decline` and `afterGrowth` at V06 §3.2's places. V06's `'history'` strategy registers a phase for each of V06 §2.1's twenty steps that runs anything: it reuses the base phases of `demand`, `dossier`, `lapse` and `character` and the base part of `prelude`, wraps the base parts of `prelude`, `field`, `siting`, `growth` and `works` with its own acts, and adds `hazards`, `uses` ((b)), `departures` and `decline` ((c)), `fortification`, `terrainWater`, `raisedWays`, `ladder` ((d)) and `close` (V06 §3.1 (2))".

issues.claim: Who leaves at a fall. Base §4.11 *Survivors* — *The epoch's order* (c) still reads "the strike pool (below) draws per building, deciding whose households leave first, and strikes fabric by its exposure (item 28 (f) with item 8; J-A28.45)". V06 §3.5.1 (the departure matching: the roster's suffix matched by band to exposure-weighted dwellings by `k = u^(1 ÷ w)` keys on `EVO_DEPARTURES`, with the swap rule and the protected-building refill) states "Which dwellings empty is decided by this matching; the strike pool strikes fabric only (§4.11 step (c), item 479)". f item 479 (BCR-V6-23) is the ruled base change; the base text is the pre-change one. Two different draws decide which buildings empty. (The canon routed f item 479 to rendering, by the f file's §12.6 heading; its text edits §4.11 (c), the pipeline's.)
issues.required_change: At pipeline, §4.11 (c): Apply f item 479: "which dwellings empty is decided by the evolution engine's departure matching (V06 §3.5.1: the roster's suffix matched to exposure-weighted dwellings by band), and the strike pool (below) strikes fabric only, by its exposure (item 28 (f) with item 8; J-A28.45)".

issues.claim: The use step's closing durations. Base §4.11 *Uses across epochs* (2) reads "closes only when its catchment's demand … has been below `closeShare` for `closeAfterEpochs`, or a hard supply edge has had no provider in reach for `starveAfterEpochs`". Those two fields no longer exist: §10.2's `UseRuleRow` (f item 429 (b), applied) carries `closeAfterYears` and `starveAfterYears` with `moveChance` per year, and V06 §2.9 / §3.9.4 close a use when its `Use.strain` of kind `demand` has lasted `closeAfterYears` (or `supply`, `starveAfterYears`), read on the weekly clock (J-V6.26). f item 429 (c) is the ruled base text; the base keeps the epoch counts, so the base's use step counts epochs (irregular on the weekly clock) where V06 counts years.
issues.required_change: At pipeline, §4.11 *Uses across epochs* (2): Apply f item 429 (c): "closes only when its `strain` (§2.7; V06 §2.9) of kind `demand` has lasted `closeAfterYears`, or of kind `supply` `starveAfterYears`, read on the weekly clock".

issues.claim: The regrowth-first rule and the history engine's stage exceptions. Base §4.11 *Regrowth-first* ends "an epoch whose residual is ≤ 0 grows no stage and adds no face" with no exception, and lists only tiers (0)–(6). V06 §3.6 grows a stage for the overflow backlog (`R + B ≥ q`) and a decrowding stage (`C ≥ max(q, growth.crowdShareMax × H)`) — "the two exceptions item 336 states" — and V06 §3.8.2 places tiers (5′) (upgrade of downgraded ways, reopening of hollow ways) and (5″) (crowding) between the base's (5) and (6), with the reopen-on-placement rule at every placement, again citing the base ("Tiers (5′) and (5″) are this strategy's own tiers between the base's (5) and (6) (item 336)"). f item 336 (BCR-V6-18) is the ruled base text and is absent: the base's absolute rule forbids what V06 builds. (The canon routed f item 336 to determinism, by the f file's §5.3 heading; its text edits §4.11, the pipeline's.)
issues.required_change: At pipeline, §4.11 *Regrowth-first*: Apply f item 336: after "an epoch whose residual is ≤ 0 grows no stage and adds no face" add "— the owner-staged history engine's two exceptions excepted (V06 §3.6): a stage for the overflow backlog, whose households are those its overflow ladder housed in earlier epochs, and a decrowding stage, whose households are the crowded ones it moves. That engine places its own tiers between (5) and (6): (5′) the upgrade of downgraded ways and the reopening of retired ones (V07's hollow ways, `reopenWay`) and (5″) crowding within a factor of the band row (V06 §3.8); and every placement that engine makes — at every tier, in its use step's openings and moves, or in a dossier-backed use's relocation — on a plot whose access edge is a retired way reopens that way, with any retired way on its path to the ways in use, in the same batch first (V06 §3.8.2)".

issues.claim: Which buildings cast in an epoch's daylight term. Base §4.5 *The daylight term* ("at an epoch the previous epoch's buildings do (V06 §3.4)") and §4.11 (a) ("the previous epoch's buildings casting in the daylight term") restate V06's rule as "the previous epoch's buildings". V06 §3.4 (1) — the home of the building shade mask — writes the mask from "the buildings as they stand when the field phase runs — after this epoch's hazards" (a quarter a fire opened is sunnier at once, J-V6.29), before anything the epoch's later phases place. After a fire or a topple in the epoch's `hazards` step the two statements give different casters (a burned building casts at its eave, a toppled one at its ruin share).
issues.required_change: At pipeline, §4.5 and §4.11 (a): Replace the restatement by the rule's reference: "at an epoch the buildings standing when its field phase runs — after that epoch's hazards, before anything it places — cast through V06's building shade mask (V06 §3.4)"; §4.11 (a) likewise ("the buildings standing at the field phase casting through the building shade mask (item 102 (e); V06 §3.4)").

issues.claim: The decline table's slower dwell bands are undefined numbers and disagree with the layers' own lag rules. Base §4.11's decline table (f item 291's row) reads "walls, raised ways and retaining walls one band slower, tunnels two", and II.6 "its dwell bands are two steps slower than a building's"; "one band slower" and "two" are given no years anywhere. Their readers disagree on what they time: V06 §3.19.2 (3) strikes a raised span "whose dwell band has run since the way's neglect" (which band, unstated); V04 §3.10's `UndergroundFade.candidates` takes elements "whose dwell band has run (§4.11's persistence table: the `underground` row and its bands)" (no band in `UndergroundFadeRule`); while an enceinte's stretches are breached at `walls.breachChancePerYear` from the neglect with no dwell band (V06 §3.7.3) and a retaining stretch is a candidate after V11 §3.18's `retaining.neglectAfterYears` (30) with no dwell band (V06 §3.19.4 (3), V11 §3.18). Two builders would give different lags to the same layer.
issues.required_change: At pipeline, §4.11's decline table, dwell-band row; II.6's tunnel sentence citing it: State the row exactly, the specific layer rules qualifying the general: "vacant → derelict [10, 30]; derelict → ruin [20, 60]; ruin → cleared on salvage demand only. A raised way's span: a standing span is a strike candidate once [20, 60] years — drawn once per span, keyed with the epoch of the way's neglect — have run since that neglect (V06 §3.19.2 (3)). A tunnel, gallery or chamber: each step once [40, 120] years — drawn once per element and step, keyed with the epoch it entered its condition — have run (V04 §3.10). An enceinte's stretches step by V06 §3.7's pathway rows (`walls.neglectAfterYears`, `walls.breachChancePerYear`, `walls.dismantleChancePerYear`), and a retaining stretch after V11 §3.18's `retaining.neglectAfterYears`, with no further band." (The two numeric bands are the base's own band progression shifted one and two places — [10, 30], [20, 60], [40, 120] — our own, calibratable, §13.9; if the editor reads "one band slower" otherwise, the row must still give the years.) V04 §3.10 and V06 §3.19.2 (3) then cite the row by these words.

issues.claim: V06 states two different memberships of the strike pool and a wall lag the wall rules do not have. V06 §1.1 (4) lists "the per-layer candidates of the base's strike pool (building, plot boundary, street, wall)", while V06 §3.5.2 says "Enceinte walls are not in the pool (their pathway is V06 §3.7's)" and V06 §3.7.2 (3) repeats "V06 §3.5.2's exclusion of enceinte walls from the pool stands"; V06 §3.19.2 (3) calls the raised kind "one dwell band slower than buildings, as walls", but no wall rule of V06 §3.7 reads a dwell band (AT-07). The base's persistence row (`wall` 0.05) is read only as V06 §3.7.3's stretch weight factor.
issues.required_change: At V06: §1.1 (4) reads "the per-layer candidates of the base's strike pool (building, plot boundary, street, and item 110's raised, retaining and deck kinds), an enceinte's stretches stepping by the fortification phase's pathway (V06 §3.7)"; §3.19.2 (3) drops "as walls" and cites the dwell-band row as AT-07 words it.

issues.claim: The catacomb primary's tie rule. V04 §3.5.1 (5) — the home of the primary reading — takes "the complex whose source serves the most burials — the greatest need `A` of (2) …, ties by rank … at every derivation; at an epoch, V06's derived primary, the same reading held by its hysteresis". V06 §3.18.2 (3a) breaks the tie "by source address". With two complexes of equal served burials the epoch and a regeneration pick different primaries, so the rank cap holds a different complex — the opposite of "the same reading".
issues.required_change: At V06 §3.18.2 (3a): "the primary is V04 §3.5.1 (5)'s reading — the complex whose source serves the most burials, ties by rank — held by `catacomb.primaryHysteresis` (10 %): another complex becomes the primary only when its served burials exceed the current primary's by that share".

issues.claim: A burial source's age after epochs. Base II.7.6 (the age gate's home, `minAgeYears` 100) gives "a source's age is its own — at generation `(K − k + 1) × yearsPerStage` …, after the replay or epochs the log's years since its use opened", which for a source standing at generation drops its generation age once an epoch runs. V06 §3.18.2 (2) (the epoch's reader) adds them: "`(week − burialsBegan) ÷ 52 +` its generation age … the generation age II.7.6's stage age at creation or the port's `HistoryHint.ageYears`", and V04 §3.5.1 (3) reads "`minAgeYears` by the face's growth stage, `HistoryHint` or the log". A churchyard 150 years old at generation is 10 years old after a decade of epochs by the base, 160 by V06 — the age gate opens or not by which text is built.
issues.required_change: At pipeline, II.7.6's age sentence: "… at generation `(K − k + 1) × yearsPerStage` for a source built in growth stage k of K …; after the replay or epochs, that generation age (zero for a source opened after creation) plus the log's years since its use opened (V06 §3.18.2 (2))".

V06 §3.18.2 (1) says "Each candidate face takes V04's one uniform `u` keyed by (`catacomb`, the face's lineage) on `sewer`", the candidates including the quarry ossuary; V04 §3.12 keys a quarry ossuary's chance by its working ("the quarry ossuary's chance (`sewer`, the working)"; the fixed-key exceptions: "a quarry ossuary's by its working"). issues.claim: The hollow ways' ops are declared nowhere. Base §2.8 (*the decline and regrowth hooks*) and §7.1's village binding row say the ways' ladder runs "by `DeclineOp`'s `retireWay`, `effaceWay` and `reopenWay` (§4.11)"; V06 issues them (`ProductEpochRows.street.op`/`again`/`reopen`, V06 §2.1; the village street candidate, V06 §3.5.2; tier (5′) and the placement rule, V06 §3.8.2; the replay's destroy, V06 §3.20.5 (1)) and V07 issues and hand-binds them (V07 §3.12, §4.1, §4.4). §4.11's `DeclineOp` union has no such member: f item 268 (BCR-V7-32) part (b) — the ruled member — is missing, so the `convert` operator has no op for any of the three. (The canon routed f item 268 to model, by the f file's §2.8 heading; model applied part (a), and part (b) edits §4.11, the pipeline's.)

issues.claim: The replay's destruction uses the hollow-way op outside its domain and outside its build slot. V06 §3.20.5 (1) has "every way takes `retireWay` (V07's op, item 268 …)" at a destroy effect. The base restricts the op to "ways on ground part 0 of the land classes … at a village rung" and says "the crossing and water classes (`bridge`, `pier`, `quay`, a mole) and every raised part never become hollow ways … a `ford` retires with its carried way" (§2.8; f item 268's member: "never on a deck, a ford or a raised part"). And item 268 is STAGED with the village product (V-M), while V06 §8's E9 (the replay) names no dependency on it; with no village product registered V06 §3.3.2's clamp ([1 500, 120 000]) forbids the destroy's "target 0 from `w` until the refounding".

issues.claim: Whether the base's own epoch path re-resolves `Features.sewers`. II.7.1 says the feature is "re-resolved at each epoch against the epoch's rung and population … (V06's prelude, V06 §3.2; the first epoch it turns on, the network is laid whole, §4.11)", and §4.11 *Regrowth-first* (6), a `'grow-by-stage'` rule, lays the network whole "the first epoch the feature turns on … (V06's `under.extend`)". V04 §8's V4-U5 builds "U-NET laid whole at the first sewers epoch … run by hand and on M4's grow path", and V04 §3.10 has `SewerStrategy.extend` "on the grow-by-stage path, after the new stage's S11". But V06 §3.1 (2) defines `'grow-by-stage'`'s `prelude` as "the rung and the dials before S2" only — the re-resolution is V06's — so on M4's path (no V06) a TOWN grown past CITY's floor never turns sewers on and V04's first-sewers-epoch contract has no caller. Two units place one rule in different strategies.

issues.claim: The V06 half of AT-14: V06 §3.1 (2) lists `'grow-by-stage'`'s `prelude` as "(the rung and the dials before S2)", and V06 §3.2's *The feature set at an epoch* presents the re-resolution as the engine's, so under `'grow-by-stage'` (T-V6-1's arbiter, "a step M4 runs that has no phase fails it") the feature is never re-resolved, against II.7.1 and V04 §8's V4-U5.
issues.required_change: At V06 §3.1 (2) and §3.2: §3.1 (2): "`prelude` (the rung, the dials and the feature set before S2)"; §3.2 *The feature set at an epoch* opens "The base's prelude act (II.7.1; item 550), run under both strategies: …", the first-epoch whole-network clause naming V04's M4 hook on `'grow-by-stage'` beside `under.extend`.

issues.claim: The stage component of `hood.fabric`'s draws. V06 §2.1 (`EpochParticipant.stage`: "its draws' stream-key stage and its reads' tag") and V06 §3.16 ("participants register the stage their volume names — … `S9b` for `hood.fabric` … and their draws use that id") put every draw of the participant on stage `S9b`. V01 §3.3.6 registers `stage: S9b` but draws "on `ctx.stream(S7c | S9b, entity)`" — S7c's rule for a new district on `S7c`, S9b's rule for a re-cut block on `S9b`. A new district's fabric draw takes a different stream key by each text.
issues.required_change: At V06 §2.1 and §3.16: `EpochParticipant.stage`'s comment reads "the stage its volume names (V06 §3.16) — its reads' tag and its draws' default stage; a participant that runs two stages' rules draws each on that rule's stage through `ctx.stream(stage, entity)`"; §3.16's list reads "`S9b` for `hood.fabric` (V01 §3.3.6: its S7c rule draws on `S7c`, its S9b rule on `S9b`)".

issues.claim: `Way.surface`'s lifecycle row omits its epoch writer. V01 §2.7 — the field's home row, which V06 §2.12 cites ("V01's field (V01 §2.7; item 207), this volume one of its epoch writers") — gives `create` "S10a's end (V01 §3.7.3)" only, while V01 §3.7.3 itself and V06 §3.4 (9) have the epoch's `field` phase write it ("a `setAttr` (cause `rule:field`) written where the value changes"), and V06 §2.10/§2.12 the landfall clearance's `setAttr` pair (V06 §3.5.2). The home row and its readers disagree on who writes the field.
issues.required_change: At V01 §2.7, the `Way.surface` row: `create` reads "S10a's end (V01 §3.7.3); at an epoch the `field` phase's re-lay (a `setAttr` op of the `epoch` event, cause `rule:field`; V06 §3.4 (9)) and the landfall clearance's `setAttr` pair (cause `rule:landfall`; V06 §3.5.2)"; `undo` reads "the writing event's undo record (an epoch's for the engine's writes)".

issues.claim: The `hood.fabric` participant's scope is stated twice in V01 with different scopes. V01 §3.3.6 (its home) gives (1) districts made outside S7b → S7c, (2) every block of `EpochScope.recut` ("re-cut or redeveloped" by rung 3) → S9b, (3) the districts `scope.raised` crosses, (4) nothing else; V01 §3.5.11 restates it as S9b "on the blocks an epoch creates outside a growth run's S10a hook and on due blocks rung 3 redevelops" — a block set (blocks outside S10a's hook) §3.3.6 does not list, and "redevelops" without "re-cut". V06 §3.2's participant table follows §3.3.6.

V02 §3.14.1 (a) says "at an epoch (§4.11) the previous epoch's buildings enter the daylight-share raster through them"; V06 §3.4 (1), the mask's home, rasterises "the buildings as they stand when the field phase runs — after this epoch's hazards", before anything the epoch's later phases place (the pair of AT-06 in the base). issues.claim: The dig-from-above draw's key at an epoch. V04 §3.5.7 (d) — the draw's home — keys it by "(the building's lineage, `dig`, the void kind; the lineage carries the epoch that built it and the wing key of a wing V02's mutator adds, V02 §3.9 W6)", and V02 §3.9 W6 has an added wing draw "once for an access down, keyed (building lineage, `dig`, the void system's kind, the wing's key)". V06 §3.18.1 (2a) restates the key as "one uniform per (building lineage, `dig`, void kind)" and says only "a rebuild on a trace … and every new stage's buildings bring new draws", so a `MutationPlan` step or a rung-3 op that adds a wing over a void (`scope.basementGrown`) re-compares the building's old draw instead of drawing for the wing.
issues.required_change: At V06 §3.18.1 (2a): Replace the restated key by the reference: "its fixed-key draw (V04 §3.5.7 (d): key parts the building's lineage, `dig` and the void kind, with the wing key of a wing the mutator adds, V02 §3.9 W6) … while a rebuild on a trace (a successor lineage, §6.3), a wing an epoch's mutation adds and every new stage's buildings bring new draws".

issues.claim: Which crypts the rank counts. V03 §3.7.4 (3) — the rank's home — runs it "over every building with a crypt", the principal being "the `cathedral` building's … with no cathedral, the `always` building's with the largest ring". V06 §3.18.3 (2) adds a condition the home lacks: "Only crypts of buildings whose **live** use is in the church family are ranked; a vacant, ruined or converted building's crypt stays in the model, unranked." After an epoch ruins or vacates a former cathedral, V03's text keeps it principal and caps the live see's crypt; V06's makes the live seat principal. One rule, two homes, two results.
issues.required_change: At V03 §3.7.4 (3): The rank's opening reads "Only crypts of buildings whose live use is in the church family are ranked — a vacant, ruined or converted building's crypt stays in the model, unranked (the epoch case, V06 §3.18.3 (2)). The settlement's principal crypt is the ranked `cathedral` building's …"; V06 §3.18.3 (2) then cites V03 §3.7.4 (3) for the condition instead of stating it.

issues.claim: The village street candidate's rate. V07 §3.12 *Decline and desertion* says a disused way "is a candidate of the pool's `street` kind at a village rung … struck at V06 §3.5.2's street rate **per year** over the epoch's span (`1 − (1 − p)^years`, §4.11 *The clock* (5))". V06 §3.5.2 — the pool's home — makes the persistence rate a layer weight: "`w = E(x) · rate(layer) · u` …, strikes are taken in descending `w` … with no second draw … until the district's `fabric` churn cap or the 2-plots-per-block bound stops it"; V11 §3.18 repeats that the rows are "a layer weight inside the churn cap …, never a per-year chance" (J-V11.71).
